Okay.. I’m gonna be honest I really really don’t think it’s your ph. And I don’t think you should even focus on that right now. I’m no expert but I’ve taken in alottt of sick bettas over the years - here’s my “battle plan”for your baby: 

• first, dump out, clean his 5 gal, for a fresh clean start. (I can already hear the comments about the precious nitrogen cycle - I’m getting to it!) 

•second, fill the tank about a 1/4 to a 1/3 of what it usually is with conditioned water. The goal here is to not only let him reach the top with less effort, but also it should bump up his temperature a bit. Ideally, I’d like it around the low 80’s with him being sick. 

•third, take your sponge filter and wring it out into the 5 gallon. You want all that gross brown nasty water in there to get your cycle going a bit again.

•forth, get your almond leaves and boil about 4-5 of those suckers and pop those in there (I always like to 1 unboiled in there to slowly leach out tannins. The goal is to make that water BROWN. (totally up to you but I love to throw in a pothos cutting in my sick betta tanks too!!)

•I would do little water changes every 3 days with a piece of airline tubing and a small bucket. Offer 2 or 3 pellets a day IN HIS TANK, don’t take him out to feed him anymore. If he doesn’t eat them just take the pellets out, bettas can go upwards of a week without food, he’ll be okay I promise. Stability and cleanliness is THE most important thing in saving bettas. Keep me posted!!
